process_area.title: Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations

value_stream.name: Employee Transport, Shuttle & Daily Commute Management

fields.Trigger: Need assessment (W4241); route review; new-store opening (VS-37)
fields.Volume: Routes per site × shift; pickup points across the employee catchment

workflows.name: Shuttle Route Design, Shift Schedule & Pickup-Point Network

Automation Opportunity: - Route-optimization/clustering tools; ridership-vs-capacity auto-alerts; schedule publication to ESS/app
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: routes evidence-designed (geocoded); schedule shift-aligned; reviewed periodically
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-19.3/VS-103.3 (shifts), VS-06 (fleet/route), VS-37 (new-store), W4241 (need), W4263 (re-optimization)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Route-inefficiency risk**: Long detours inflate cost/time; mitigated by cluster-based design + re-optimization (W4263)
- **Shift-misalign risk**: Shuttle arrives late → attendance/OT impact; mitigated by schedule aligned to roster with buffer
System Touchpoints: - Route/ridership analytics (VS-28); shift roster (VS-19.3/VS-103.3); fleet/route tool (VS-06); site data (VS-07)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks per route-design cycle; ongoing re-optimization

steps.activity: Transport/Analytics design routes balancing employee home-cluster coverage, pickup-point safety/accessibility, travel time, shift start/end alignment, and vehicle capacity — using the geocoded need (W4241) and traffic/route data
Transport define the published schedule (route, stops, times) per shift, communicate to riders and site managers, and align arrival/departure to shift roster (VS-19.3)
Transport periodically re-optimize routes on ridership/traffic change (W4263), manage route changes/disruptions, and keep the pickup-point network documented

fields.Volume: ~6,762 employees; majority of store/DC shift staff boarding daily

workflows.name: Daily Shuttle Dispatch, Manifest & Passenger Check-In

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile manifest with QR check-in; GPS arrival/departure auto-log; ridership→analytics/payroll feed
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: manifest enforced (no unentitled boarding); seat-belt/no-overload; trip closed & reconciled
Cross-references: - links to VS-103.1 (ESS/app), VS-06 (dispatch), VS-23 (security gate), W4251 (entitlement), W4252 (pre-trip), W4253 (allowance), W4264 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overload/unsafe risk**: More riders than seats; mitigated by manifest check-in + no-overload rule (W4260)
- **Unaccounted-rider risk**: Non-employees boarding; mitigated by ID/QR check-in vs entitlement (W4251)
System Touchpoints: - Manifest/ridership module; ESS/app QR check-in (VS-103.1); fleet dispatch (VS-06); security gate (VS-23)
Time Estimate: - ~5–10 min boarding per trip; dispatch ongoing

steps.activity: Dispatcher generates the daily trip manifest (route, driver, vehicle, expected riders from W4251), confirms vehicle/driver readiness (pre-trip W4252), and dispatches on schedule
Driver/Coordinator board employees against the manifest (check-in — employee ID/ESS QR), enforce seat-belt/no-overload, and log actual riders/departure/arrival times
Coordinator closes the trip (actual manifest, no-shows, exceptions), flag issues (overcapacity, refused boarding), and feed ridership data to analytics (W4264) and payroll/allowance (W4253)

fields.Volume: Entitlement records for eligible employees × route/shift

workflows.name: Employee Entitlement, Ridership Eligibility & Seat Allocation

Automation Opportunity: - Policy→entitlement auto-derivation; HRIS event-driven entitlement updates; waitlist/seat auto-allocation
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: entitlement policy-driven (W4242); synced to HRIS lifecycle (VS-19/VS-103); audited vs ridership
Cross-references: - links to VS-19/VS-103.1 (HRIS/ESS/lifecycle), VS-103 (shared services), W4242 (policy), W4245/W4249 (capacity/routes), W4264 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ghost-rider risk**: Entitlement retained after exit/transfer → boarded by others/fraud; mitigated by HRIS sync on hire/transfer/exit + ridership audit
- **Allocation-fairness risk**: Waitlist management perceived unfair; mitigated by transparent allocation rule
System Touchpoints: - HRIS/ESS entitlement (VS-19/VS-103.1); ridership register; capacity (W4245); policy (W4242)

steps.activity: HR/Transport determine each employee's transport entitlement from policy (W4242 — shift, role, site, distance), assign to route/seat, and maintain the ridership register in HRIS/ESS
Transport allocate seats against capacity (W4245/W4249), manage waitlists and alternates, and update on hire/transfer/exit (VS-19.1/VS-103)
HR/Transport handle entitlement exceptions (temporary eligibility, route-swap request), approve per policy, and audit entitlement vs actual ridership (W4264)

fields.Trigger: Daily operations; driver hire (VS-19.1); compliance cycle
fields.Volume: Driver pool covering all routes × shifts

workflows.name: Driver Roster, Qualification & Daily Pre-Trip Operations

Automation Opportunity: - Digital pre-trip checklist; license/clearance expiry auto-alerts; fatigue/hours tracking; fitness-to-drive attestation
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: drivers licensed/cleared/medically fit (DOLE); pre-trip completed; hours/fatigue managed (VS-24)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06.2 (fleet/driver), VS-24 (HSE), VS-19 (HR/driver record), VS-23 (clearance), W4260 (compliance/pre-trip), W4255 (incident)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unfit-driver risk**: Fatigued/unlicensed/unfit driver → accident; mitigated by fitness-to-drive check + fatigue/hours management
- **Credential-lapse risk**: Expired license/clearance; mitigated by re-credentialing registry (W4260)
System Touchpoints: - Fleet driver mgmt (VS-06.2); HSE (VS-24); HR/driver record (VS-19); security clearance (VS-23)

steps.activity: Fleet/Transport maintain the driver roster and qualifications (professional driver's license, PNP/LTO clearance, medical/DOLE fitness, defensive-driving training), with re-credentialing tracking
Driver performs the daily pre-trip (vehicle condition check per W4260, fuel, first-aid/fire extinguisher, manifest/IDs), and Dispatcher confirms fitness-to-drive (not fatigued/intoxicated)
Dispatcher/HSE manage driver hours/fatigue, incident records (W4255), and performance coaching; escalate unfit drivers

fields.Trigger: Eligibility (W4251); payroll cycle (VS-19.2); monthly vendor/rideshare billing
fields.Volume: Allowance recipients + service-vehicle assignees + rideshare/vanpool participants

Automation Opportunity: - Allowance auto-compute from rate table; payroll-vs-ridership exclusion check; fuel-card spend analytics
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: allowance BIR-coded (W4243); entitlement exclusivity enforced; fuel/personal-use controlled (VS-61)
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-102 (comp), VS-61/VS-06.2 (fuel/fleet), VS-34 (procurement), VS-17.4 (finance), W4243 (rates), W4251 (entitlement), W4264 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Double-dip risk**: Employee claims allowance + boards shuttle; mitigated by entitlement exclusivity (W4251) + payroll-vs-ridership reconciliation
- **Fuel-abuse risk**: Service-vehicle fuel misused; mitigated by fuel card controls (VS-61) + personal-use logging
Time Estimate: - Part of payroll cycle; ~1–2 days monthly reconciliation

steps.activity: Payroll compute and pay the transport allowance to eligible non-shuttle employees per rate table (W4243), with BIR tax coding, in the semi-monthly run (VS-19.2)
Fleet/Transport administer the service-vehicle program (assigned vehicles, fuel card per VS-61, personal-use policy/logging) and the rideshare/vanpool program (subsidy, platform, eligibility)
Finance/Transport reconcile allowance, fuel, and rideshare/vanpool spend, validate against policy/actuals, and feed cost analytics (W4264)

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Security (VS-23), Labor Relations (VS-84), Site Managers
fields.Trigger: Night-differential shifts (10 PM–6 AM); close/open shifts; special events/seasonal peaks
fields.Volume: Employees on after-dark shifts, with emphasis on women-safe service

Automation Opportunity: - GPS live-tracking with SOS/panic; geofenced safe-drop confirmation; after-dark incident analytics
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: after-dark/women-safe standard enforced (VS-24); SOS available; close/open coverage guaranteed
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-23 (security), VS-06 (GPS), VS-19.2 (OT), VS-84 (labor), W4255 (incident), W4263 (improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Safety risk**: After-dark assault/harassment at stops/in vehicle; mitigated by women-safe standard + escort/SOS + monitored stops
- **Coverage risk**: Late shifts uncovered → staff stranded; mitigated by guaranteed close/open coverage
System Touchpoints: - HSE (VS-24); security/CCTV (VS-23); fleet GPS (VS-06); SOS/panic integration; payroll OT (VS-19.2)
Time Estimate: - Standard definition ~2 weeks; daily ops ongoing

steps.activity: Transport/HSE define the after-dark service standard (door-to-door/drop-point safety, escort/wait-until-safe protocol, CCTV-monitored pickup points, GPS-tracked vehicles) prioritizing women-safe transport
Transport ensure late-night coverage (vehicle/driver availability for close & pre-open shifts, overtime per VS-19.2), and the SOS/emergency-contact procedure (links W4255)
HSE/Security monitor after-dark incidents, audit compliance with the women-safe standard, and improve routes/stops on feedback (W4263)

fields.Participants: Driver, HSE (VS-24), Security (VS-23), Insurance (VS-26), HR (VS-83), Legal (VS-100)
fields.Trigger: Vehicle breakdown; road accident; medical/security incident en route

Automation Opportunity: - In-vehicle SOS/automatic crash notification; incident→HSE/insurance workflow; CAPA tracking (VS-133)
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: incident SOP followed; passenger-liability insured (VS-26); root-cause CAPA logged (VS-24/VS-133)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE/CAPA), VS-06 (fleet), VS-26 (insurance), VS-23 (security), VS-83 (clinic), VS-100 (legal), W4260 (corrective), VS-133 (CI)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Passenger-harm risk**: Inadequate response worsens injury/liability; mitigated by SOP + first-aid + emergency linkage
- **Liability risk**: Uninsured/undocumented incident; mitigated by passenger-liability insurance (VS-26) + incident logging/CAPA
System Touchpoints: - HSE/incident system (VS-24); fleet (VS-06); insurance/claims (VS-26); security (VS-23); HR/clinic (VS-83)

steps.activity: Driver/Coordinator execute the incident response (secure scene, passenger safety first-aid, notify Dispatcher/HSE/Security, call emergency services if needed) per the transport incident SOP
HSE/Fleet investigate (root cause, driver/vehicle factors, road/weather), arrange alternate transport for stranded passengers, and log to the HSE/incident system (VS-24)
Insurance/Legal handle claims/passenger-injury (VS-26), corrective action (driver retraining/vehicle repair W4260), and reporting/CAPA (links VS-24/VS-133)

fields.Participants: Transport Lead, Site Managers, Payroll (VS-19.2), HR (VS-103)
fields.Trigger: Employee inquiry/complaint; missed shuttle; route-swap; lost item
fields.Volume: Inquiries across the workforce (ride issues, schedule, allowance)

workflows.name: Transport Helpdesk, Employee Inquiry & Exception Handling

Automation Opportunity: - ESS self-service case logging; chatbot for FAQ (schedule/routes); auto-dispatch of backup; SLA dashboard
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)
- CTL-654: cases logged/tracked to closure; SLA monitored; safety escalations to HSE (VS-24)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103.1 (case/ESS), VS-06 (dispatch), VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-28 (analytics), VS-24 (HSE), W4248 (EX), W4263/VS-133 (CI)
- links to VS-103.1 (case/ESS), VS-06 (dispatch), VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-28 (analytics), VS-24 (HSE), W4248 (EX), W4263/VS-133 (CI)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-staff risk**: Missed-shuttle inquiry unresolved → absence/safety; mitigated by backup-dispatch SLA
- **Recurring-issue risk**: Themes unaddressed; mitigated by CI feed (VS-133) and EX analytics (W4248)
System Touchpoints: - HR case/ESS (VS-103.1); dispatch (VS-06); payroll (VS-19.2); analytics (VS-28); HSE (VS-24)

steps.activity: Helpdesk receive employee transport inquiries (missed shuttle, route/stop request, lost item, allowance dispute, safety concern) via ESS/call/hotline, log a case, and triage
Helpdesk resolve or route the case (dispatch a backup, arrange alternate transport, escalate safety to HSE W4254/W4255, route payroll to VS-19.2), and track to closure
Helpdesk analyze recurring issues (missed shuttles, complaint themes), feed CI (W4263/VS-133) and EX (W4248), and report SLA performance

fields.Frequency: ~2–5 disruption events per year across the operating regions (transport-group strikes recur with modernization policy cycles; flood-season road closures are annual); most resolve within one day, the rare multi-day event is the tail case
fields.Owner: Transport Lead / Fleet Planning (VS-06) (continuity protocol); Site Managers (attendance execution)
fields.Participants: Store/DC Managers (site staffing decisions), HR Shared Services (VS-103.1 attendance & leave placement), Regional Managers (multi-site calls), Fleet Dispatch (shuttle surge per W4250), Payroll (VS-19.2, attendance coding), VS-19.3 (scheduling), Communications/VS-63 (employee & customer messaging), Regional Manager closure authority (the E-02 custody where trading cannot be sustained)
fields.Trigger: A citywide or regional commute interruption threatening mass absenteeism on a trading day — a PUV/jeepney strike or transport-group protest, major-flood or landslide road closures on primary commute corridors, or a fuel-supply disruption idling commuter transport across a metro where BuildRight concentrates stores and a DC
fields.Volume: 1 event × the affected metro's sites (30–80 stores + 1 DC) × the affected sites' crews (typically 30–60% of store headcount commutes by public transport) × the trading day's staffing requirement

Automation Opportunity: - Attendance-impact forecast model keyed to commute-mode profiles and corridor status feeds (replaces manual Step 1 estimation)
- One-tap transport-disruption attendance code in the WFM app with payroll-rule auto-apply (replaces manual Step 6 coding)
- Shuttle-surge manifest template with consolidated pickup points pre-computed per corridor scenario (replaces ad-hoc dispatch)
- Store-locator/app status flags driven from the event record (replaces phone-tree status calls)
Background: The corpus owns the site and the vehicle: typhoon/flood protocols (W576/W848/W1387) protect *stores*, W850/W2510 decide whether a *site* opens, W4255 responds to a *shuttle* incident, and W484/W854 handled pandemic attendance — but nobody owned the commute-interruption event, where every site is open and reachable-yet-unstaffed: the crews cannot get in. A PUV-modernization-class strike strands 30–60% of a metro store's crew with zero damage to the building; the flood-closure variant strands crews on the far side of impassable corridors. The event needs an owner for the attendance-forecast call, the skeleton-crew and critical-role matrix (cashiers, keyholders, receiving), the shuttle-surge and pickup-consolidation plan, the ride-share/allowance activation under W4253, the attendance coding that keeps payroll honest, and the customer-impact decision riding the existing closure custody.
Controls: - CTL-654 (ensure controlled execution — Shuttle Service, Route & Daily Commute Operations (PA-141.2).)

- operational: attendance coding under a declared commute disruption uses the no-penalty category verified against the event record; surge transport runs on W4250 manifests with W4253-gated allowances; any trading-day closure rides the E-02 custody and is documented either way
Cross-references: - links to W4250 (shuttle surge manifests), W4251/W4253 (commute profiles & allowance activation), W4255 (vehicle-level incident boundary), W561/W10 (attendance & payroll coding), VS-63/VS-75 (status messaging), VS-103.1 (leave placement), W2510/W850 (E-02 closure custody), W576/W848/W1387 (site-protection boundary — the event targets the commute, not the site)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-staffed-trading risk**: opening on a skeleton crew without setting service expectations produces queue failures and safety issues at lumber-yard loading; mitigated by Step 4's explicit service-level matrix
- **Penalty-absence risk**: stranded crews charged with unexcused absences, driving grievance and attrition; mitigated by Step 2's no-penalty coding directive and Step 6's payroll integrity
- **Keyholder single-point risk**: the one keyholder stranded closes the store regardless of crew; mitigated by Step 2's critical-role matrix with cross-trained backups
- **Ad-hoc-transport risk**: managers improvising unreimbursed pickups; mitigated by Step 3's W4253-gated allowance activation with manifest discipline
- **Silent-closure risk**: a store silently unopened while signage says open; mitigated by Step 5's status push and the E-02 custody documentation
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed by site management, HR Shared Services, Payroll and the transport program; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Workforce-management attendance codes with the transport-disruption category and no-penalty flag (links to W561/W10)
- Shuttle dispatch console with surge manifests and consolidated pickup points (links to W4250)
- Ride-share/allowance activation record under the W4253 entitlement rules
- Store-communication cascade and app/store-locator status flags (links to VS-63, VS-75)
- Closure-decision record where trading cannot be sustained (links to the E-02 custody, W2510/W850)
- Corridor-vulnerability register keyed to the site roster for pre-planning
Time Estimate: Per event day ≈ 30–60 minutes per affected site for the staffing call and messaging (≈ 15–30 staff-hours per 30-site metro) plus 4–8 hours of transport-coordination and payroll coding centrally; at the 2–5-events-per-year cadence this stays absorbed within site management, HR Shared Services and the transport program — no incremental headcount.

steps.activity: **Disruptor & scope call**: classify the event (strike vs flood-closure vs fuel) from news/authoritative feeds; map affected corridors against the site roster; forecast attendance impact per site from commute-mode data (W4251/W4253 profiles)

**Attendance directive**: site-level staffing directive — report-if-you-can with no-penalty absence coding for stranded crews; critical-role matrix activates (keyholders, cashiers, receiving; department minimums)

**Continuity transport**: shuttle surge on consolidated pickup points (W4250 manifest discipline), ride-share/van-pool allowance activation per W4253 for critical roles, carpool coordination via the site channels

**Trading decision**: open-with-skeleton-crew is the default with service-level expectations set (lane count, services suspended); where staffing or safety cannot sustain trading, closure rides the E-02 custody — W2510's decision matrix, W850's mechanics; documented either way

**Customer & employee messaging**: opening status and service levels pushed to store channels, app/store locator and local social; employees get the transport options and the no-penalty confirmation in one communication

**Payroll & leave integrity**: attendance coding per the directive (transport-disruption code — no absence-hit, no unverified absent); partial-day attendance tracked; the coding rides W10-class payroll rails

**After-action**: attendance-vs-forecast reconciliation, shuttle-surge utilization, corridor vulnerability register update (chronic corridors pre-plan consolidated pickups), and the multi-day playbook refresh
